name: Javier Milei
description: Argentine president associated with radical market liberalisation, spending cuts and socially conservative positions.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Competitive elections and constitutional institutions coexisted with extensive executive decrees.
axes.counter: Congress and courts constrained some proposals; radical policy is not abolition of elections.

axes.brief: Economic and personal liberty coexisted with strict controls on obstructive protests.
axes.counter: Restrictions on gatherings and order distinguish practice from maximal libertarian rhetoric.

axes.brief: A shared Argentine identity accompanied individual equality rhetoric.
axes.counter: Exact accommodation spending and cultural exceptions are not established.

axes.brief: First-year liberal economic rhetoric provides open-movement context.
axes.counter: Later 2025 immigration restrictions are excluded; welfare eligibility analogies remain uncertain.

reasons.14: His rejection of compulsory welfare funding provides specific counter-evidence: entry for individual opportunity does not imply tax-funded benefits or social housing for non-citizens.

axes.brief: US and Israeli alignment and defence capability coexisted with limited intervention.
axes.counter: Foreign-policy rhetoric does not demonstrate every preventive-war threshold.

axes.brief: National autonomy and rejection of socialist international blocs coexisted with Western alignment.
axes.counter: Proposed dollarisation qualifies the usual nationalist currency preference.

reasons.10: The proposed dollarisation explicitly contemplated surrender of discretionary national monetary issuance. National-sovereignty rhetoric cannot override this monetary exception.

axes.brief: Broad privatisation proposals preferred private enterprise and service delivery.
axes.counter: Congressional limits and retained enterprises qualify realised implementation.

axes.brief: Trade opening and reduced barriers followed free-market arguments.
axes.counter: Implementation was gradual and some taxes and controls remained in 2024.

axes.brief: Deregulation, market prices and monetary alternatives were central priorities.
axes.counter: Some controls persisted temporarily; direction is assessed rather than every realised outcome.

axes.brief: Austerity and individual property arguments opposed redistribution as a general aim.
axes.counter: Targeted child and food assistance increased, qualifying rejection of every transfer.

reasons.12: Targeted child and food assistance increased in the first year despite broad cuts. The support clause is plausible, while his stated opposition to redistributive entitlement makes unqualified agreement implausible.

axes.brief: Religious language and conservative values coexisted with civil legislative institutions.
axes.counter: Personal faith does not imply a clerical veto or religious courts.

axes.brief: Opposition to abortion and progressive gender policy reflected social conservatism.
axes.counter: Legal non-interference in private relationships differs from social acceptance.

axes.brief: Market-led technical development was favoured over precautionary economic restriction.
axes.counter: No exact endorsement of risky embryo or neural enhancement was established.

axes.brief: Federal institutions and reduced central spending support some local fiscal responsibility.
axes.counter: Presidential decrees and national enforcement complicate decentralising rhetoric.

axes.brief: Individual choice and rejection of structural explanations coexist in his rhetoric.
axes.counter: Market beliefs do not imply biological race explanations; these comparisons are weakly evidenced.
